physics_goals.quote: WA97 was the first experiment in high-energy physics which made use of this new technique.
physics_goals.value: Measure strange and multi-strange baryon and antibaryon production in lead-lead collisions to test the predicted strangeness enhancement

summary.plain: WA97 was a CERN experiment in the SPS West Area that studied strange and multi-strange particles in lead-lead collisions using a new silicon pixel telescope placed near the target. It was the first high-energy physics experiment to use that technique, and found enhanced strangeness production.
summary.technical: WA97: heavy-ion experiment in the Omega spectrometer (West Area) with a seven-layer, 0.5 million channel silicon pixel telescope plus ten microstrip planes measuring hyperon production in Pb-Pb, p-Pb and p-Be collisions at 158A GeV/c (1994-1996); observed the enhancement of multi-strange baryons increasing with strangeness content; succeeded by NA57.
